standard.title: Sort and record information
standard.description: sort and record information including pictorial timelines and locations on pictorial maps or models
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have informal sorting experience from everyday life. No formal prior HASS inquiry skills curriculum.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students sort and record information using pictorial timelines and pictorial maps or models.

nodes.label: Sorting information
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can sort provided sources (photographs, objects, drawings) into categories relevant to an inquiry question.
nodes.minimum_width: Sort at least four items into two categories using a provided sorting rule (e.g. old/new, near/far, same/different).
nodes.typical_width: Sort a range of sources (photographs, drawings, objects, mementoes) into relevant categories for a HASS inquiry; explain the reason for sorting decisions.
wider: Create their own sorting categories for a set of sources and explain the reasoning behind their categories
Sort sources chronologically and explain what the ordering reveals about change over time
nodes.hinge_reason: Sorting is the prerequisite for recording — students who cannot sort into categories cannot build a meaningful pictorial timeline or map in the following node.

response_modes.reason: Sorting requires practice with physical materials before moving to recording. Use hands-on manipulation of photographs, cards and objects before expecting students to translate sorting into a recorded format.

success_criteria: Sorts at least four items into two categories using a provided rule
Can explain why an item belongs in a particular category

nodes.label: Pictorial timelines
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can add photographs or drawings to a pictorial timeline in the correct sequence, representing events from their own life or a familiar story.
nodes.minimum_width: Sequence at least three photographs or drawings on a provided timeline, placing them in correct time order.
nodes.typical_width: Add photographs or drawn representations of significant events to a pictorial timeline; create a timeline of events over the year or key family events; explain the sequence.
wider: Compare two timelines (e.g. their own timeline vs a family member's) and identify events that appear in both
Create a class timeline of significant shared events, discussing how to decide what goes on it

response_modes.reason: Sequencing is a new cognitive demand at Foundation — practise with clearly ordered physical events before adding less familiar or ambiguous items.

success_criteria: Places at least three items on a timeline in correct sequence
Can explain why one item comes before or after another

nodes.label: Locations on pictorial maps or models
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify features on a provided pictorial map or model of a familiar place and link drawn representations to their real-world locations.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two features on a provided pictorial map of a familiar place (e.g. school map) and match them to pictures or drawings of those features.
nodes.typical_width: Use a provided pictorial map or oblique aerial photograph to find and link multiple features to pictures; describe the location of features using simple spatial terms (near, beside, opposite).
wider: Add a new feature to a pictorial map using a symbol or drawing and explain its location relative to existing features
Compare a pictorial map with a photograph of the same place and identify similarities and differences

response_modes.reason: Maps integrate sorting (what features are there) and location vocabulary into a spatial record — this is the node where both come together in a representational format.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two features on a provided pictorial map
Links at least one map feature to a drawing or photograph of that feature
